strategy_name: Noise band · v4 entry cap, lookback 1–32 (5m + 15m)

strategy.summary: Trade breakouts from the day's normal range, flat by the close. For every time of day the strategy averages how far price has been from that day's open over the last N sessions; times the band multiple, that is the noise band around today's open. At each check time a close above the band goes long and a close below it goes short, at the next bar's open. The position trails out through the band, the session VWAP, or whichever is closer, and is always closed at the session's last close. After Zarattini, Aziz & Barbon (2024).
strategy.formula: band = open ± multiple × average |close − open| ÷ open at this time of day over the last N sessions (× today's open)

rules.label: Enter
rules.text: At a check time (every 15, 30 or 60 minutes from the open, and not before the first-entry time), buy when the bar closes above the upper band and sell short when it closes below the lower band. The order fills at the next bar's open. The gap-adjusted anchor starts the upper band from the higher of the open and the prior close, the lower band from the lower.

rules.label: Exit
rules.text: At a check time, exit when price closes back through the band, through the session VWAP, or through whichever of the two is closer, filled at the next open. Anything still open is closed at the session's last close. No stop loss in this round.

rules.label: Size
rules.text: Long, short or both; one position at a time, never held overnight; optionally capped at 1 or 2 entries per session. As many whole ES contracts as the account covers at full contract value (no leverage), starting from $1,000,000.

strategy.length_note: The band lookback counts trading days; check and first-entry times are minutes after the open.

funnel.name: Start
funnel.why: All 13,824 versions backtested once on 2018–2022 data.

funnel.name: 1 · Integrity
funnel.why: Per-trade checks for look-ahead, impossible fills and overnight holds on every version, plus 40 random versions re-run on cut-off data. 0 failed.

funnel.name: 2 · Enough trades
funnel.why: Needs ≥100 completed trades and ≥10 a year in ≥4 of the 5 years. Removed 0 (none).

funnel.name: 3 · Profit
funnel.why: Needs a net profit, Sharpe ≥ 0.75 and drawdown no worse than 30%. Removed 10,824 (5,432 on 5min, 5,392 on 15min); 1,363 of them lost money.

funnel.name: 4 · Stable settings
funnel.why: Each setting is nudged one at a time, down and up: band lookback by ±20% (rounded) and band multiple by ±0.25. At least 70% of the nudged versions must be profitable, with median Sharpe ≥ 0.5. Removed 9.

funnel.name: 6 · Remove duplicates
funnel.why: Versions whose monthly returns correlate ≥ 0.8 form a group; the best 2 of each go on (a group of one keeps its one). 2,920 versions formed 164 groups; 300 of the 326 picks are distinct backtests (first-entry times before the first check act alike).

funnel.name: 8 · Validation
funnel.why: Frozen finalists run once on unseen data: needs net > 0, Sharpe ≥ 0.3, drawdown no worse than 30% and ≥40 trades.

luck.method: Per bar size and direction setting: random intraday trades on random sessions at random times, never overlapping and always closed by the session's last bar, covering the target share of the validation window's bars. Trade lengths are drawn from that group's own validation trades; each trade is long with the group's actual long share (1.0 for long-only), else short. Same fills, slippage, commission and whole-contract sizing as the strategy; scored with the same daily-Sharpe and time-in-market code.
luck.text: For every whole-percent time in market in each group's 2023–2024 range, 100 random runs trade ES at random times on random days. Each group is one bar size and direction setting. Like the strategy, the random trades are intraday only, never overlap, and are always closed by the session's last bar. Their lengths are drawn from that group's own finalist trades, so trade counts and costs match. Long-only groups trade long; long-and-short groups go long with the same share of trades their finalists did. They pay the same costs and use the same sizing and Sharpe math as the strategy.

assumptions: Data: Databento CME continuous front month (ES.v.0), 1-minute bars aggregated to 5 and 15 minutes. Rolls are back-adjusted so the roll gap is not treated as a price move; the band is scaled by the real (unadjusted) open.

Day session only: NYSE regular session 09:30-16:00 NY on NYSE trading days. Overnight Globex trading is not used: "the open" is the day-session open and the prior close is the previous day-session close. Nothing is held overnight.
Costs: 1 tick slippage per side and $2.50 commission per contract per side, including the session-close exit.
The paper sizes by volatility with up to 4× leverage; here each trade uses the whole account in whole contracts with no leverage, the same as the mean-reversion runs.
Session VWAP is built from the 5- or 15-minute bars' typical price and volume, not ticks.
After an exit, a new entry in the same direction waits until price closes back inside the band at a check time; the opposite direction isn't blocked.
With no stop, 5- and 15-minute bars decide at the same check times, and a first-entry time before the first check changes nothing, so the grid contains exact duplicates; they collapse in stage 6.
Sharpe uses daily mark-to-market returns (√252), with idle cash earning 0%. Time in market is the share of bars with an open position.
Holdout (2025 onward) has not been run. It is a one-time final test and needs an explicit go-ahead.
